    Latest Update: Norse Atlantic Cancels All Flights As Norwegian Operating Firm Files For Bankruptcy

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Norse Atlantic has canceled all flights and stopped selling tickets after its Norwegian operating firm decided to file for bankruptcy.
    • Norse Atlantic declared today, November 27, 2026, that the board of its Norwegian operating subsidiary, Norse Atlantic Airways AS, will file bankruptcy petition with the Agder District Court in Norway.
    • The organization could not secure sufficient funding to meet its immediate cash needs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Norse Atlantic has canceled all flights and stopped selling tickets after its Norwegian operating firm decided to file for bankruptcy. Efforts to save the remaining business continue, but for passengers with upcoming bookings, the immediate reality is grim. Another airline built around affordable longhaul travel has run out of money, further calling into question the sustainability of the low-cost business model.

    Norse Atlantic declared today, November 27, 2026, that the board of its Norwegian operating subsidiary, Norse Atlantic Airways AS, will file bankruptcy petition with the Agder District Court in Norway.

    The organization could not secure sufficient funding to meet its immediate cash needs. Its board concluded that continued operations at the Norwegian subsidiary were no longer viable. The publicly listed parent, Norse Atlantic ASA, and other group companies are outside this filing. Management is still seeking a solution for the remaining business, including the UK and USA subsidiaries.

    But all flights are canceled and ticket sales have ended. CEO Eivind Roald said:.

    “We are deeply sorry for the impact this has on our passengers, employees and partners.”.

    The bankruptcy announcement followed another serious development earlier today.

    According to recent reports, according to Reuters, the lessors of all 12 aircraft in the Norse fleet sent notices terminating their lease agreements. Norse disputes the validity of those notices.

    That leaves the remaining business facing an enormous challenge. Finding new financing is difficult enough. Resolving access to the aircraft needed to operate the airline adds another obstacle.

    The deterioration has been rapid. On November 25, Norse warned that its financial situation was critical. It suspended flights the following day. Today came the lease termination disclosures and the decision to put the Norwegian operating company into bankruptcy.

    I’m not optimistic about this carrier ever flying again.

    When I first wrote about Norse in 2021, I welcomed the prospect of another airline offering inexpensive transatlantic flights after Norwegian abandoned longhaul service.

    According to recent reports, my enthusiasm was primarily about competition. Even travelers who never booked Norwegian benefited when its fares forced larger airlines to respond. I hoped Norse could provide similar pressure while avoiding the problems that had undermined Norwegian.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier this year, I covered Norse withdrawing from Los Angeles as fuel costs surged. Cutting routes that could no longer support themselves seemed sensible, even as it raised concerns about how much room the airline had left to maneuver.

    Reuters identifies soaring fuel costs associated with the Iran war as a major pressure on the business. That is a brutal challenge for an airline trying to sell inexpensive tickets on flights that spend many hours in the air. World’s “most famous” flight attendant, Sara Nelson, a Marxist who seemingly aspires to higher office herself, blamed the Iran war:.

    On Thanksgiving, the war with Iran means U.S. based @afacwa Flight Attendants, and all Norse Atlantic workers, are facing losing their careers. All flights are suspended. Crew are traveling home w/ livelihoods hanging in the balance. @ITFglobalunion https://t.co/x7SDrvL5DI.

    — Sara Nelson (@FlyingWithSara) November 26, 2026.

    But the broader difficulty with this model remains. A low advertised fare can fill seats without producing enough revenue to sustain the operation. Charging separately for meals and bags helps, but the airline simply could not sustain fares high enough to break even.

    Established network carriers have advantages that are difficult to replicate, including connecting traffic and customers willing to pay substantial premiums for flexible schedules or premium cabins.

    In a recent development, if you have an upcoming Norse booking, the airline has confirmed that all flights are canceled. If you’re left with a cancelling itinerary, contact your card issuer about the options available for a canceled service (if you paid extra for travel insurance, you can start there). If you booked through a travel agency or as part of a package, contact that provider too.

    There will be plenty of people saying this outcome was predictable. Indeed it was, but that offers little comfort to employees facing uncertainty or passengers whose plans have fallen apart.

    Norse gave travelers another option. Losing that option is disappointing even for those of us who generally preferred to fly on other carriers. I hope something viable can emerge from the remaining business. But another temporary infusion of cash into an operation that will soon need the same help again would be foolishness.

    Norse Atlantic has canceled all flights and ended ticket sales as its Norwegian operating subsidiary moves to file for bankruptcy. The parent company and UK business remain outside that filing, with efforts to secure a future continuing.

    For now, passengers need alternative travel arrangements, and employees face an uncertain future. I welcomed Norse because more competition benefits travelers. I am sorry to see it reach this point, even if the warning signs have been visible for some time.

    • Industry observers note that if you hold Marriott Bonvoy elite status and aren't going to requalify for your status tier this year, there's good news: The program is extending its “soft landing” policy into 2027.
    • Related: Marriott elite status: What it is and how to earn it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's that time of year again: Your last chance to plan your final flights or mattress runs of 2026 in order to snag last-minute elite status for next year.

    Industry observers note that if you hold Marriott Bonvoy elite status and aren't going to requalify for your status tier this year, there's good news: The program is extending its “soft landing” policy into 2027. With this policy, if you fail to requalify for your current status this year, you will only drop one tier from March 2027 until February 2028.

    Related: Marriott elite status: What it is and how to earn it.

    Based on the program's elite-status policies, the Marriott Bonvoy status you earned in 2025 will expire at the end of February 2027 unless you requalify for your current level or higher in 2026. But what if you don't meet the threshold for the same or higher status?

    That's where Marriott's generous soft landing policy comes in. Whether you qualify for a level far below your current status or don't qualify for status at all in 2026, you'll only drop one status tier in 2027.

    According to Marriott's website, members who don't requalify for status will see their upcoming, lower tier take effect in early March 2027, and they can enjoy this status through February 2028. Meanwhile, if you requalify for your existing tier or a higher tier, you will also hold this status through February 2028.

    This soft landing policy, which Marriott has offered for years, is a win-win: It provides valuable benefits to elite members who weren't able to requalify for status, while giving them a reason to stay loyal to Marriott and perhaps try again for status next year.

    Related: The complete guide to earning Marriott elite status with credit cards.

    Marriott Bonvoy elite status offers some excellent perks, such as room upgrades, late checkout and even lounge access. Thankfully, with this soft landing policy, mid- and upper-tier elite members who don’t requalify this year won’t be left empty-handed. You can still enjoy the benefits of the next-lower tier from March 2027 to February 2028.

    For example, with Titanium Elite status, expiring Ambassador Elite members will enjoy many of the same perks of their current status, including complimentary breakfast at most brands, suite upgrades at check-in, 75% bonus points earned on stays and a status match to United MileagePlus Premier Silver status.

    You should see your new Marriott status and updated expiration in early March.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that cathay Pacific became a Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer partner on November 18.
    • Recent findings suggest that cathay Pacific has announced higher mileage requirements for selected airline partner awards ticketed beginning January 5, 2027.
    • Cathay is also eliminating Companion Ticket Awards from the same date.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that cathay Pacific became a Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer partner on November 18. One week later, it announced that selected partner award tickets will cost more Asia Miles beginning in January. As much as I celebrate the addition of Cathay Pacific to Chase, the timing offers a useful reminder: the value of flexible points depends on what you can actually book with them.

    Recent findings suggest that cathay Pacific has announced higher mileage requirements for selected airline partner awards ticketed beginning January 5, 2027. The increases vary by route and cabin. Several of the published examples rise by 20%, while some longhaul business class awards increase by roughly 8% (see my table below).

    Cathay is also eliminating Companion Ticket Awards from the same date. Standard Awards and Upgrade Awards on Cathay Pacific itself are unaffected by this announcement. The separate oneworld multi-carrier award chart is also unchanged.

    VFTW highlights the increases, including the following examples shared by Cathay.

    These are one-way prices per passenger and represent selected changes rather than a complete fresh partner award chart:.

    For example, British Airways first class from Los Angeles to London will increase from 135,000 to 162,000 Asia Miles. For two passengers, that is another 54,000 miles for the same one-way journey….

    That is a substantial increase, especially when taxes and surcharges are still payable in addition to the miles (book BA with JAL miles to avoid the surcharges).

    Industry observers note that cathay attributes the changes to higher costs charged by its partner airlines. I understand that redeeming miles for a seat on another carrier involves an expense for the program, though it is also my understanding that partners actually pay very little for out of pocket for these seats (see this OMAAT post).

    Chase added Cathay Pacific as a transfer partner on November 18, with eligible Ultimate Rewards points transferring to Asia Miles at a 1:1 ratio, a positive development for Chase cardholders.

    More ways to compare award prices and access seats are useful, and this devaluation does not erase the value of having Cathay available. Still, announcing higher partner award prices a week later takes some of the shine off the news (not that I am claiming any collusion!).

    Someone who saw the latest transfer option and moved points into Asia Miles without a particular redemption in mind now has a deadline to consider: it is exactly why I do not transfer points unless I am ready to immediately book.

    In a recent development, A bank point that can become miles in several programs gives you options. Once transferred, it becomes subject to the pricing and availability of the receiving program.

    That flexibility has value. I say this often, but keep your points flexible as long as you can.

    Perhaps Asia Miles offers the best deal today. By the time you are ready to book, another program may offer a lower price or access to a more convenient flight. Keeping the points in a flexible currency account like Chase Ultimate Rewards allows you to make that comparison when it actually matters.

    Of course, there are circumstances in which a transfer bonus or a specific booking opportunity makes moving points worthwhile, but it has to be very compelling if I’m going to move points over without booking.

    In a recent development, cathay indicates the current mileage requirements remain available for tickets issued through January 4, 2027, at 11:59 pm Hong Kong time (for U.S. readers, that is 10:59 AM Eastern). The deadline concerns when the ticket is issued, rather than when you travel. You can book a later trip at the current price if award space is available and the ticket is issued before the cutoff.

    Cathay also says date changes to those tickets can retain the original mileage requirement after the increase, subject to award availability and applicable change fees. Other changes will be subject to the revised mileage requirements.

    I appreciate the advance notice very much. If you have a trip in mind and find the seats, there is an opportunity to act before the increase.

    Cathay Pacific is increasing selected partner award prices beginning January 5, 2027, shortly after becoming a Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer partner.

    Industry observers note that the Chase addition remains welcome, and Cathay-operated Standard Awards are unaffected by this announcement. But the higher partner prices make some redemptions less attractive. This news once again reinforces the value of keeping bank points flexible until I am ready to book…don’t transfer until you are ready to book.

    Tempers flare as future of Social Security debated

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).
    • If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday revealed how poisonous the politics could become.
    • Sources indicate that budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday revealed how poisonous the politics could become.

    Sources indicate that budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

    According to recent reports, “I think it’s outrageous,” stated Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking vital.”.

    Recent findings suggest that johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

    In a recent development, "This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he said on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”.

    But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”.

    In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson mentioned Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”.

    Industry observers note that johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he said.

    Industry observers note that there is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson remarked Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

    And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

    Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

    In a recent development, A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a proposal in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

    Sources indicate that senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

    Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

    “I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability issue, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” mentioned Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Review: United Airlines 737 MAX 8 Economy Class Newark To Nuuk, Greenland

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • My United Airlines flight from Newark to Nuuk, Greenland featured a friendly crew, two meal services, and a spectacular approach onboard a Boeing 737 MAX 8 in economy class.
    • Greenland had been on my bucket list for years, and United’s nonstop service from Newark offered an opportunity to finally visit.
    • Recent findings suggest that I had already traveled from Palm Springs through San Francisco and Denver to reach Newark.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    My United Airlines flight from Newark to Nuuk, Greenland featured a friendly crew, two meal services, and a spectacular approach onboard a Boeing 737 MAX 8 in economy class. Economy Plus was perfectly comfortable for the four-hour daytime journey, though the flight became much fuller than I had expected thanks to a large contingent of United employees taking advantage of their travel benefits.

    Greenland had been on my bucket list for years, and United’s nonstop service from Newark offered an opportunity to finally visit. I was heading back to Germany to pick up my children after their summer visit with family and decided to take a rather scenic route via Nuuk and Copenhagen.

    Recent findings suggest that I had already traveled from Palm Springs through San Francisco and Denver to reach Newark. By the time I boarded this flight, I was tired…but very excited about what lay ahead.

    I booked the entire United itinerary from Palm Springs to Nuuk using 40,000 Air Canada Aeroplan points, plus $5.60 in government taxes and the CAD39 partner booking fee.

    A cash ticket for the itinerary was about $1,600, so I was pleased to use miles instead. The premium cabin on the Greenland flight, marketed as Premium Plus, was sold out when I booked (and I don’t mean no saver partner award space, but sold out completely).

    My overnight flight from Denver arrived at the A Gates, and the Nuuk flight would depart from the same terminal.

    There was a United Club nearby, but I wanted a shower and barista-made coffee, so I took the airside shuttle bus to Terminal C and visited the United Club near gate C123. I wrote separately about that visit. There was no wait for a shower, and although I would have preferred hotter water and stronger pressure, it was refreshing to clean up after the redeye.

    An illy double-shot cappuccino helped too. I had breakfast, got some work done, and then returned by bus to the A Gates about 30 minutes before boarding.

    This turned out to be a much more energetic flight than I expected.

    Recent findings suggest that the night before departure, the flight appeared less than half full. By the time we pushed back a few minutes late, it was much closer to capacity, with a large number of United employees traveling on standby.

    Sources indicate that I initially had an Economy Plus row to myself, but two jovial United employees joined me. They were heading to Greenland for just one night. As I explained in my first impressions of the flight, several employees described arriving in Nuuk, exploring town, taking a twilight boat excursion, and visiting a bar before returning to the airport for the morning flight back to Newark.

    That sounded absolutely exhausting to me, but I understood the appeal. If I had those travel benefits, I would certainly be tempted to use them on a route like this! There was certainly a festive atmosphere onboard, and I enjoyed hearing how others planned to spend their short time in Greenland.

    Boarding was delayed 20 minutes, but it was finally time to step onboard.

    According to recent reports, I was warmly greeted by Craig, the purser, as I boarded. More on him below.

    In a recent development, united’s 737 MAX 8 features 150 seats one economy class in a 3-3 configuration. Seats are Collins Meridian slimline seats and feature an adjustable headrest and seatback screens. Legroom is 30 inches (34 inches in Economy Plus), the seat is 17 inches wide, and seats recline two inches.

    I selected a window seat on the left side of the aircraft in Economy Plus.

    There are individual air nozzles onboard as well as seatback power (A/C under the seat and both USB-A and USB-C under the screen).

    The window seat on the A side proved an excellent choice during our approach, though the best side will depend on which direction the aircraft lands, which will depend on the winds.

    Despite a flight time of only about four hours, there were two services during the flight.

    Recent findings suggest that I had ordered United’s “balanced diet” special meal, which consisted of chicken pieces in tomato sauce accompanied by a side salad, bread roll, and “That’s It” fruit snack for dessert. It was not exactly gourmet, but it did the job and I had some club soda to drink with it.

    It has been revealed that the regular choices for passengers were pasta or beef. Is the diet meal worth ordering?

    As we approached Nuuk, I received an Indian vegetarian wrap (other passengers received a pizza pocket). It was not necessary for such a short flight, but appreciated nevertheless. I enjoyed a cup of illy coffee as well.

    In a recent development, united’s seatback screens feature a deep content of movies and TV shows with a handful of game and audio options. The same library of content was also available via streaming to your own device.

    Complimentary earphones were provided, though you could pair your own device to these screens, which I did.

    The flight featured Viasat Wi-Fi, available for purchase for $10 ($8 for MileagePlus members) and it worked well over the Atlantic.

    United’s 737 MAX 8 has one lavatory in the front for premium cabin passengers and two in the back for economy class, which is not a great proportion.

    The purser, Craig, was a highlight of the flight.

    Recent findings suggest that apparently, he worked nearly every Nuuk flight that summer and has become something of an institution on the route. He was friendly, professional, and knowledgeable, making his way through the cabin and chatting with passengers.

    We had a nice conversation about restaurant recommendations in Nuuk. I appreciated speaking with someone who knew the destination and could offer advice before I arrived. What a fun assignment to spend the summer flying to Greenland!

    In a recent development, A good crew can make an ordinary flight enjoyable, and Craig helped make this unusual route feel even more special. Between the enthusiastic employee travelers and his warm welcome, the mood onboard was very pleasant.

    The highlight came during our descent.

    In a recent development, I had chosen an “A” window seat on the port side, which gave me a northerly view during our final approach. Aircraft can arrive from the opposite direction depending on the wind, so the view will vary, but I was very happy with my choice.

    It has been revealed that as we descended below the clouds, tundra and floating ice came into view. Then the sun broke through, revealing the mountainous landscape around Nuuk.

    I have flown over Greenland many times, looking down from cruising altitude and wondering what it would be like to visit. Seeing it from this perspective, knowing I would soon be on the ground, was quite different.

    Recent findings suggest that some of the mountains still held snow, and the landscape looked rugged and sparsely populated. It was majestic.

    Recent findings suggest that I shared more photographs in my earlier post about the approach. My arrival in the Faroe Islands a couple of years earlier may have been even more scenic, but this was nevertheless a wonderful welcome to Greenland.

    This is a flight where I would strongly recommend a window seat.

    We landed at 7:08 pm local time under clear skies and taxied to a parking position outside the terminal.

    Air Greenland-branded stairs were brought to the aircraft, and we walked down onto the apron. It was about 55ºF outside…crisp, clear, and beautiful.

    After the long journey from Southern California, I was finally in Greenland.

    Next came immigration, which turned out to be a story of its own.

    > Read More: My Longest EES Immigration Wait Yet Was In Tiny Nuuk, Greenland.

    In a recent development, this was such a fun flight. Economy Plus was comfortable for the relatively short daytime journey, Craig provided excellent service, and the atmosphere onboard was cheerful…it almost felt like an inaugural flight. The approach into Nuuk was the highlight and made me very glad I had selected a window seat on the A side (though again, I was fortunate because the approaches change based on prevailing wind conditions).

    According to recent reports, getting to Newark had required several flights and an overnight journey from Denver, but this final segment was a pleasure. I was thrilled to finally reach Greenland and appreciated being able to do so on United.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A subsidiary of China Southern Airlines has agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft, Reuters reported Tuesday.

    The airplanes, which have a total list price of $7.4 billion, will be used by Xiamen Airlines, which is based in Fujian. Deliveries are expected from 2031 to 2034.

    It has been revealed that the deal is Boeing’s largest with a Chinese operator in nearly a decade. The country largely shifted toward Airbus aircraft as relations with the U.S. frayed.

    In a recent development, president Donald Trump hoped to reverse that trend during his state visit to China in May. Trump discussed a potential purchase directly with Chinese President Xi Jinping, and even brought along Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg for the summit. Ultimately, Beijing agreed to buy 200 aircraft from Boeing, fewer than analysts expected, but still notable considering Boeing’s drought in the country.

    In a recent development, trump said earlier this week that he thinks China will buy 250 more aircraft from Boeing. He did not provide details or say where that information came from.

    China Southern stated the new aircraft will help Xiamen expand after it relocates to the new Xiamen Xiang’an International Airport. The facility will replace Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport as Xiamen’s main gateway.

    5 tips to maximize rewards and avoid debt this holiday shopping season

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Although the holiday season can be joyous, it can be an expensive time of year, with gifts, travel and gatherings putting extra pressure on your budget.
    • But with a little planning, you can make the most of your credit card rewards and benefits without overspending.
    • Here are five tips to help you save money and earn rewards like a pro this holiday season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Although the holiday season can be joyous, it can be an expensive time of year, with gifts, travel and gatherings putting extra pressure on your budget.

    But with a little planning, you can make the most of your credit card rewards and benefits without overspending.

    Here are five tips to help you save money and earn rewards like a pro this holiday season.

    First, map out your holiday shopping prepares and set a realistic budget for spending. Who are you shopping for? How much are you planning to spend on gifts? What other expenses should you factor into your holiday budget?

    These are all good questions to help you set expectations and prevent impulse buys that can lead to overspending.

    Sources indicate that A spreadsheet is a great way to keep track of spending and budgeting. You can simply insert your budget into a premade template or write it down on paper. If you already know what you proposal to buy, insert links to the sales pages so you know how much it will cost.

    While adjusting and finalizing your budget, remember to factor in additional costs due to extra gatherings, like larger grocery and dining expenses.

    One of the best things about rewards cards is that they often come with perks to help you save money.

    Before making your holiday purchases, check whether your credit cards offer statement credits or other benefits that could help you save money.

    Sources indicate that for example, comes with an up to $75 quarterly statement credit (up to $300 annually) Lululemon credit that can be used at U.S. stores (excluding outlets) or online after enrollment. This is a great way to maximize purchases on clothing, yoga gear or other accessories.

    Or, if you have a frequent jet-setter in your life, you can use a credit card’s Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit to cover their application fee of up to $120.

    Statement credits aren't the only card benefits worth checking before you shop. For an expensive electronic device or other high-value gift, purchase protection or extended warranty coverage are other useful perks.

    According to recent reports, we talk a lot about shopping portals during this time of year. That's because skipping them is essentially leaving money on the table.

    By doing your online holiday shopping through a portal, you can earn bonus points or cash back at a massive number of online retailers. Most of the major U.S. airlines have shopping portals to help you earn additional miles on every eligible purchase, or you can use third-party portals such as Rakuten to earn cash back or Amex Membership Rewards or Bilt Points.

    Industry observers note that we suggest using a shopping portal aggregator like Cashback Monitor to find the best portal for each online purchase. That way, you don’t have to sift through each portal’s offers individually.

    Recent findings suggest that no matter where you shop, review any Amex Offers, Chase Offers or Citi Merchant Offers available on your cards. They vary by cardmember, and often stack with your card's standard rewards plus a shopping portal. Some require activation or enrollment before making a purchase.

    Related: Everything you need to know about credit card merchant offers.

    According to recent reports, we’re substantial fans of points and miles at The Points Guy — and for good reason. Points and miles can reduce the cost of future travel, but cash-back cards may be more useful if you want rewards to offset your holiday expenses directly.

    A flat-rate cash-back card such as the (see rates and fees) is an easy way to earn rewards no matter where you shop since it offers 1% cash back when you make a purchase and another 1% cash back when you pay your bill. Redeeming those rewards as a statement credit helps reduce the size of January's bill.

    The (see rates and fees) is another great option that earns at least 1.5% back on every purchase.

    Related: Best cash-back credit cards.

    It has been revealed that paying your statement balance in full is generally best, but some rewards credit cards offer a 0% introductory annual percentage rate period on latest purchases. That can give you time to pay for a planned expense without interest as long as you have a plan to pay it off completely before the introductory period ends.

    In a recent development, another option is to use one of the financing options some credit card issuers offer. Amex Initiative It® and Chase Pay Over Time after purchase may allow eligible cardmembers to divide qualifying purchases of $100 or more into fixed monthly payments, generally with a fixed monthly fee instead of interest.

    You’ll almost always save money using these programs compared to paying interest over time.

    Related: Chase Pay Over Time and My Chase Loan: Should you opt in?

    Sources indicate that holiday shopping doesn't have to derail your budget. By planning ahead, using the right rewards cards and taking advantage of statement credits and shopping portals, you can make your spending more rewarding without buying more than you can afford.

    It has been revealed that the key is to prioritize your budget over earning points, miles or cash back. After all, the value of those rewards can rapidly disappear if you're carrying a balance and paying interest.

    ICAO Hosts Air Transport Conference, Elects Fresh Council Members

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Airlinegeeks

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Last week, ICAO headquarters in Montréal hosted the Seventh Worldwide Air Transport Conference, where member states and industry stakeholders gathered to set global policy priorities on aviation economic regulation, infrastructure financing, resilience, consumer protection, and sustainable growth.
    • Sources indicate that over 1,500 delegates from 154 member states and organizations attended the week-long event 13 years after the Sixth Conference in 2013.
    • “Broad agreement was reached on the need for harmonized, risk-based, and proportionate economic regulation that facilitates the adoption of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, automation, sustainable aviation fuels, and advanced air mobility solutions,” ICAO said in a press release during the conference.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Last week, ICAO headquarters in Montréal hosted the Seventh Worldwide Air Transport Conference, where member states and industry stakeholders gathered to set global policy priorities on aviation economic regulation, infrastructure financing, resilience, consumer protection, and sustainable growth.

    Sources indicate that over 1,500 delegates from 154 member states and organizations attended the week-long event 13 years after the Sixth Conference in 2013. They discussed high-level topics in commercial aviation: modernizing economic and legal frameworks, investing in infrastructure and skilled workforces, and ensuring that innovation keeps pace with rapidly changing technologies and global demands.

    “Broad agreement was reached on the need for harmonized, risk-based, and proportionate economic regulation that facilitates the adoption of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, automation, sustainable aviation fuels, and advanced air mobility solutions,” ICAO said in a press release during the conference.

    It has been revealed that participants agreed on the value of frameworks that support innovation and investment for economic development. They stressed this especially for smaller landlocked states, which depend heavily on air connectivity for growth.

    The conference supported modernizing air navigation infrastructure in line with ICAO’s Global Air Navigation Blueprint. It also supported liberalizing air service agreements without making liberalization conditional on infrastructure development, since new air links fostered by more liberal agreements are seen as key to economic growth.

    Industry observers note that however, all initiatives should be flexible enough to address local circumstances and should not burden developing states. ICAO’s statement continued: “The conference also reaffirmed that international standards are key to building effective, market-enabling policies and avoiding fragmentation that could impede cross-border air services. Delegates pointed to ICAO’s Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) as a successful example of this approach.”.

    Participants were asked to express their views on consumer protection legislation that has become an integral part of the legal framework for all air operators.

    At the Sixth Worldwide Air Transport Conference in March 2013, ICAO was asked to develop core principles on consumer protection. The final document, adopted by the ICAO Council in 2015, contains provisions on:.

    The report for the Seventh Conference invites states to modernize their consumer protection frameworks, keeping them evidence-based, proportionate, accessible, and responsive to the changing realities of commercial air transport. It also notes legislation should establish clear responsibilities for carriers, intermediaries, and other providers regarding information, complaints, and disruption assistance.

    Industry observers note that ICAO is expected to review its core principles while preserving national and regional flexibility. It is also expected to assess whether existing policies adequately cover online intermediaries and other overlooked situations.

    Many member states cautioned against the ICAO Air Passenger Handbook proposed by IATA, because producing and maintaining a single repository covering many different national laws would be too costly.

    The conference asked ICAO to “examine the need for harmonized, risk-based guidance on the use of AI in aviation, including common terminology and meaningful human oversight.”.

    It has been revealed that the rapid development of AI and its unknown effects on aviation operations is a topic member states will need to monitor. ICAO will coordinate and facilitate international exchange, while states will oversee implementation to ensure that the technologies adopted are secure, interoperable, and consistent with cybersecurity and data-protection objectives.

    ICAO will handle AI within its existing structure, as the proposal to create an ad hoc unit was not supported.

    In a recent development, during the final two days of the conference, ICAO held an extraordinary session of its assembly to elect the four additional council members required by the entry into force of the 2013 protocol amending the Convention on International Civil Aviation. The council is the organization’s permanent governing body, accountable to the assembly and responsible for setting priorities and implementing its directions. Its membership increased from 36 to 40, and there are no permanent seats.

    Recent findings suggest that six candidates competed for the four new seats: Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Oman, Thailand, and Turkey. In the vote on the final day, Kazakhstan and Thailand were not elected, and the other four states won seats.

    The council now comprises Angola, Argentina, Australia, Belize, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, Cuba, Denmark, Ecuador, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, Mali, Mexico, Morocco, Nigeria, Oman, Poland, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland, Turkey, Uganda, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom, the U.S., and Uruguay.

    The next elections will take place at the General Assembly in September 2028.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (621 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    How Munich Airport Clears A Runway Of Snow In Just 30 Minutes With 175 Vehicles

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With 170 vehicles and 540 personnel available for winter operations, Munich Airport (MUC) is equipped to clear each runway of snow within 30 minutes.
    • Sources indicate that MUC has reached this level of readiness in collaboration with local agricultural and trucking companies.
    • Industry observers note that MUC is so eager to show off its winter operations because of how difficult it is to keep a major international airport clear and running during the winter months.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With 170 vehicles and 540 personnel available for winter operations, Munich Airport (MUC) is equipped to clear each runway of snow within 30 minutes. These crews remain on standby around the clock from early November to mid-April, covering the months with the highest risk of heavy snow.

    Sources indicate that MUC has reached this level of readiness in collaboration with local agricultural and trucking companies. Up to 180 people can be deployed during the night shift, with the aim of keeping the runway clear of snow, ready for operations to begin in the morning.

    Industry observers note that MUC is so eager to show off its winter operations because of how difficult it is to keep a major international airport clear and running during the winter months. The airport includes two runways, with additional aprons and taxiways. This amounts to approximately 60.3 million square feet (5.6 million square meters), or 780 football fields.

    In a recent development, despite the astonishing amount of real estate MUC must keep clear to avoid delays and cancellations, the airport believes it is up to the task because it can clear each runway in just 30 minutes. It does this by deploying a fleet of 21 snow blowers, five loading snow blowers, and one snow groomer. Farmers in the local area can also be called in with snowplow-equipped tractors.

    In a recent development, MUC adds brains to the grunt task of clearing so much tarmac. Air traffic control manages the deployment and coordination of snow-clearing teams. They make use of the latest weather information and an early-warning system that intelligently predicts when icy conditions could cause a problem.

    Clear runways are pointless if the jets at an airport are too iced up to take off safely. MUC also has this accounted for with winter maintenance teams who use 'Polar Bear' de-icing vehicles, which are operated in partnership with Lufthansa. The equipment deploys de-icing fluid to ensure that a jet's wings and fuselage aren't covered in ice and snow, which could prove disastrous.

    Industry observers note that to get into the right position to deploy the fluid, the tallest 'Polar Bear' is 50 feet and 10 inches (15.5 m) tall. The maintenance team at MUC has to carefully drive these huge vehicles into the optimum position. Nadine Adden, the only woman working with the polar bears, spoke to Munich Airport's news team. She stated that:.

    Recent findings suggest that "Only when the engines and the aircraft are completely free of ice and moisture can they take off safely. (...) It's like using an oversized hairdryer. (...) I have a really cool job.".

    MUC hasn't always been a leading airport when it comes to dealing with extreme winter conditions. The airport closed twice in quick succession during the winter of 2023 after multiple days of heavy snow. On December 5, there were no takeoffs or landings from 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM. The remainder of the day saw many more flights canceled or severely delayed. Lufthansa asked its passengers to stay at home in response.

    In a recent development, the weekend before, freezing conditions had struck Europe and affected more flight operations at Munich Airport. Flight operations did not resume until 6:00 AM on Sunday, with some restrictions remaining in place for long after. Other airports impacted by this cold spell included Glasgow Airport (GLA) and Edinburgh Airport (EDI), while heavy snow in Oslo in April 2023 caused around 60 flight cancellations.

    Closures like these show why Munich Airport has invested so heavily in protecting itself from the worst winter conditions. Anything less carries a serious risk of extensive delays and cancellations, scuppering travelers' plans over the festive season and causing enormous economic damage.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Over the weekend, I booked an expensive ticket for my dad, brother, and me, from Buenos Aires (EZE) to Santiago (SCL), only to come across a better deal after I’d booked.
    • LATAM is the airline I’ve flown with the second most in my life after British Airways, my old home airline.
    • This whole situation could have been avoided if I’d been able to pay with my UK credit card on LATAM’s Brazilian website.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Over the weekend, I booked an expensive ticket for my dad, brother, and me, from Buenos Aires (EZE) to Santiago (SCL), only to come across a better deal after I’d booked. I called customer service to cancel within the 24-hour cooling-off period, but was refused a refund for the most convoluted and unnecessary reason.

    LATAM is the airline I’ve flown with the second most in my life after British Airways, my old home airline. It’s an airline I look forward to flying with for several reasons. However, this recent booking experience has uncovered a gaping hole in its customer service, which in the air I’ve always found to be excellent.

    This whole situation could have been avoided if I’d been able to pay with my UK credit card on LATAM’s Brazilian website.

    The Brazilian site has no concern when entering UK credit card details.

    However, the default setting for postcodes (ZIP codes) is numerical-only because, as in the US, Brazil’s postcodes consist only of numbers. In the UK, they’re made up of letters and numbers, so I couldn’t add the postcode that my credit card is registered to.

    I tried using only the numbers of my postcode (the one in the example above is random), but the site returned an error, saying it failed to connect to my bank. My guess would be this wouldn’t be a problem for US credit cards, given that ZIP codes consist only of numbers too.

    I remember this happening previously, but I never had an concern with a booking that I couldn’t change online.

    Ideally, I would have paid with a Brazilian bank account or credit card, but I’m still working through the immigration bureaucracy required to open one.

    First of all, I tried to cancel by logging into my LATAM Pass account, but was redirected to the contact center. This is when I realized how much of an obstacle my booking via the UK website would be.

    After being put on hold 3 times for what seemed like forever, the agent I spoke with at LATAM’s Brazilian call center told me there was nothing she could do to help me.

    Industry observers note that she explained the only way I’d get a refund was to call the UK call center, since I’d paid in GBP on the UK website. I called just before the cut-off of the 24-hour cooling-off period, so by then I had exceeded it. I had only left it so close to the cooling-off period because I was researching the trip again the following day and found a better deal; otherwise, I wouldn’t have wanted to cancel.

    If I had called sooner and had more time, I could have asked someone in the UK to call for me, as my Brazilian phone number can’t make outgoing international calls. I did top up my UK SIM Card with 20 GBP, but at a charge of 2 GBP per minute, the call disconnected after 10 minutes on hold with no answer.

    It has been revealed that irrespective of whether I could have found an easier way to contact the UK call center, I can’t help but feel that my issue should have been resolved there and then over the phone by the Brazilian call center agent. After all, I booked directly through the airline’s website, and then called the airline directly to cancel. It makes no logical sense!

    Because of a stupidly convoluted system, I’m stuck with a LATAM ticket that I can no longer cancel, even though I called customer service within the 24-hour cooling-off period.

    It’s not the end of the world, as we can still take the flights we’d originally booked, but it’s so frustrating to be put in a situation like this in 2026 because of such an archaic technicality.

    I’m still a significant fan of LATAM itself, and will continue to fly it, at least until my Platinum status runs out next year.

    Industry News: Trump banks on personal relationships moving Putin, Xi toward U.S. interests

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1233 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S.
    • That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.
    • “It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images).

    That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

    “It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

    Trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he launched a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

    Industry observers note that “We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

    They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

    In a recent development, his interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

    Both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

    Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

    “I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump said as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

    Sources indicate that “You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”.

    Trump, who was convicted by a New York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

    It has been revealed that “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump noted, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

    Other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

    And other world leaders and congressional Democrats this week expressed concern with Trump's closeness to the Russian and Chinese strongmen.

    Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., on Thursday called the unprecedented summit a “historic embarrassment.” He criticized Trump for leaving the meeting without any apparent concrete commitments from Moscow or Beijing on a number of complications, including curbing Chinese espionage inside U.S. companies and ending the Ukraine conflict.

    “This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer said.

    Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote this Thursday on X, shortly after Trump’s warm greeting for the former KGB officer: “God, protect us from such friends.”.

    Recent findings suggest that nicolas Burns, a former senior U.S. diplomatic official under GOP and Democratic presidents, was critical of Trump’s meetings with Xi. He said it was “key” for U.S. and Chinese leaders to hold talks, but added: “We need stability in the relationship with China — but there’s a but.”.

    Industry observers note that “The president seems to be following a detente policy with China, with very little substance. There’s a lot of pomp and circumstance, red carpets, a lot of nice words,” the former ambassador to China, NATO and Greece told “Morning Joe” on MS NOW. “Too friendly with Xi Jinping, who’s not going to be swayed by rosy words from President Trump.”.

    Even before Trump met with the Russian and Chinese leaders behind closed doors, Republican and Democratic lawmakers mentioned they doubted very much would come from it.

    Sources indicate that “I want nuclear weapons to be reduced. As you know, China has been unwilling to even have a conversation with the United States about nuclear arms reduction until they reach a certain plateau in the number of weapons that they have,” House Armed Services Committee Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., told reporters Tuesday.

    “I'm glad that they're willing to have the conversation. We do need a limit, as you know,” added Wittman, who lost his reelection bid earlier this month. “Right now, neither Russia nor China has a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States. It would be nice for us to actually have one.”.

    Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

    Recent findings suggest that “Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal mentioned Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”.

    On spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to quickly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

    “You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera. So, you know, in my view at least, you want to have a path forward to success.”.

    John M. Donnelly and Jackie Wang contributed to this report.

    #157259. Breaking: Norse Atlantic Files For Bankruptcy After Lessors Terminate Leases On Its 12 Boeing 787s

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (809 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Norse Atlantic Files For Bankruptcy After Lessors Terminate Leases On Its 12 Boeing 787s

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Norse Atlantic Airways' Norwegian operating subsidiary is filing for bankruptcy after the airline failed to secure sufficient emergency financing.
    • The developments follow Thursday's suspension of all flights, bringing an abrupt halt to operations just four and a half years after the airline's launch.
    • In a recent development, in a stock exchange announcement, Norse confirmed that its Norwegian operating subsidiary would file a bankruptcy petition with the Agder District Court.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Norse Atlantic Airways' Norwegian operating subsidiary is filing for bankruptcy after the airline failed to secure sufficient emergency financing. The announcement came earlier today, just hours after the carrier confirmed that it had received lease termination notices covering all 12 of its Boeing 787 Dreamliners.

    The developments follow Thursday's suspension of all flights, bringing an abrupt halt to operations just four and a half years after the airline's launch. Norse had been attempting to reinvent its business, shifting away from its original low-cost transatlantic network towards Asia and flying on behalf of other airlines.

    In a recent development, in a stock exchange announcement, Norse confirmed that its Norwegian operating subsidiary would file a bankruptcy petition with the Agder District Court. However, the listed parent manufacturer and its UK subsidiary are not included in the filing, with management continuing to explore opportunities to salvage the remaining business. Norse Atlantic CEO Eivind Roald acknowledged the impact of the decision.

    In a recent development, “We are deeply sorry for the impact this has on our passengers, employees and partners. The Board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations.”.

    Sources indicate that norse had appeared to be making progress towards profitability, reducing its annual net loss from $135.5 million in 2024 to $61.9 million in 2025. However, that improvement was dramatically reversed in 2026. Declining income coincided with rising personnel and maintenance costs, while financing expenses were exacerbated by a $32.9 million noncash charge associated with the bond conversion.

    Depreciation & Aircraft Rentals.

    Sources indicate that remarkably, Norse's fuel expenditure increased by just 2.5% in the first half of 2026, despite average jet fuel prices soaring by 92% year-on-year in the second quarter. However, beneath the surface, those spiraling costs were still taking their toll.

    According to recent reports, with no fuel hedging arrangements in place, Norse slashed its own-network capacity by 64% in the quarter, but was unable to reduce its fuel costs, widening its losses. In addition, many of its expenses remained relatively fixed, resulting in substantially higher unit costs and further undermining the economics of its scheduled services.

    In a recent development, norse secured particularly attractive aircraft leases during the pandemic, when demand for widebody aircraft had collapsed. It originally signed agreements with AerCap for nine Dreamliners and BOC Aviation for six more. Having subsequently relinquished its three smaller 787-8s, Norse operates a uniform fleet of 12 Boeing 787-9s. The airline is contesting the validity of the termination notices.

    Recent findings suggest that the aircraft could prove particularly desirable to other airlines given the current shortage of modern widebodies and the long wait times as Boeing works through its 787 backlog. LOT Polish Airlines could be a particularly logical candidate, given its existing appetite for secondhand Dreamliners.

    Original BOC Aviation Lease Duration.

    The Polish flag carrier has already secured additional aircraft previously operated by Virgin Atlantic. Other existing Rolls-Royce-powered Dreamliner operators could also represent potential destinations. British Airways, which faces delays to its Boeing 777X deliveries, could use additional 787-9s to bolster its long-haul capacity.

    Meanwhile, Thai Airways has already turned to secondhand widebodies to support its network expansion. Royal Brunei Airlines, which has ordered four additional Trent 1000-powered 787-9s, could also be a candidate if it seeks to accelerate its fleet growth ahead of those deliveries.

    There's potentially another 787 suitor that would surprise everyone: Southwest Airlines, which is reportedly considering adding long-haul flying. Adding 12 Dreamliners within months, rather than waiting in line behind competitors for years, would enable a far more rapid transformation of its business model.

    Norse introduced operations in June 2022 between Oslo and Latest York, seeking to fill the gap left by Norwegian's withdrawal from long-haul flying. However, the carrier increasingly struggled to make its original business model work. Its attention gradually shifted towards Southeast Asian destinations and aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance contracts with other airlines.

    The scale of that transformation is particularly apparent in US Department of Transportation data. Between the summers of 2025 and 2026, Norse reduced its US capacity by more than 60%, including withdrawing all its Los Angeles services. However, its load factors actually improved.

    It has been revealed that by the time Norse suspended operations on Thursday, London Gatwick–Orlando was its sole remaining scheduled US route. Meanwhile, ACMI and charter flying increased from 11% of Norse's flights in Q2 2025 to 56% in Q2 2026. Such contracts reduced its exposure to fuel prices.

    In a recent development, however, they also increased its dependence on individual airline customers. Having lost its six-aircraft IndiGo agreement, Norse secured a smaller deal with Pakistan International Airlines. Ultimately, the carrier recognized the need to reinvent its business but lacked the financial resilience to survive that transformation.
