    Citi AAdvantage Executive Card Review: Is The Admirals Club Perk Worth It?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (3975 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (formerly known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard) is American Airlines’ most premium co-branded credit card, as part of the Citi partnership.
    • Recent findings suggest that if you ask me, it’s one of the best value premium airline credit cards out there, and it’s also the airline credit card with the strongest lounge access perks.
    • In this post, I’d like to take an in-depth look at the Citi AA Executive Card, with my Citi AAdvantage Executive Card review.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (formerly known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard) is American Airlines’ most premium co-branded credit card, as part of the Citi partnership. While the Citi AA Executive Card has a steep annual fee, it offers strong perks, ranging from an Admirals Club membership, to the ability to supercharge your AAdvantage elite status, to credits that can help offset the annual fee.

    Recent findings suggest that if you ask me, it’s one of the best value premium airline credit cards out there, and it’s also the airline credit card with the strongest lounge access perks. While products like the American Express Platinum Card® (learn more) and Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card (learn more) might typically be the first that come to mind when people consider premium cards, this one could make a lot more sense if you’re a frequent American flyer.

    In this post, I’d like to take an in-depth look at the Citi AA Executive Card, with my Citi AAdvantage Executive Card review. I think this is especially key in light of the card’s recent refresh, where we saw the annual fee increase, but also saw latest perks added.

    Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard®.

    Let me start by briefly summarizing the key details of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card:.

    According to recent reports, this is the ideal card if you value American Admirals Club lounge access, if you’re going for elite status with American AAdvantage, or if you can just make the credits on the card work. If you’re just an occasional American flyer, there are probably more affordable options that will be easier to justify in the long term. However, with the card’s substantial welcome bonus, there’s a huge incentive to give this card a try.

    One of the reasons that you’ll want to consider applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the excellent welcome bonus it has. Of course that has to be balanced with the annual fee, and you also have to take into account the eligibility requirements, so let’s go through those details for the Citi AA Executive Card.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card right now has a welcome bonus of 80,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $8,000 within the first three months.

    Personally, I value American AAdvantage miles at ~1.5 cents each, so to me, those miles are worth about $1,200. That’s an excellent bonus, especially for a card that also offers a lot of value in the long run. There are so many great uses of AAdvantage miles, including for travel on partner airlines.

    For what it’s worth, I value Delta SkyMiles at 1.1 cents each, and United MileagePlus miles at 1.3 cents each, so these are the most valuable miles among the “big three” carriers, based on my math.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card bonus miles aren’t available to those who have received a latest cardmember bonus for this card in the past 48 months (however, you are eligible if you’ve had a different American Airlines credit card, including if you’ve received a bonus on a different product).

    Then there are the typical rules for Citi credit card applications, including that you can apply for at most one card with Citi every eight days, and at most two cards every 65 days.

    There’s not a consistent credit score that you need to get approved for the card, though I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that determines eligibility.

    Industry observers note that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has a $695 annual fee. There’s also a lot of value to adding authorized customers (as I’ll discuss below). You can expect to pay a total of $175 for up to three authorized users (so potentially under $60 each), and then each authorized user after that costs $175.

    Keep in mind that if you’re a Citigold customer, you can receive a $145 annual rebate on your annual fee, which is a nice perk.

    When it comes to spending money on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, here’s the rewards structure:.

    It has been revealed that in terms of the reward for spending, there are potentially better cards for purchasing airline tickets, and also better cards for everyday spending. However, keep in mind that the most compelling reason to spend money on the card is in order to earn elite status with American Airlines. American Airlines uses its Loyalty Points system for status qualification, and credit card spending can help you earn status.

    American’s elite requirements are at the moment as follows, and you earn one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on an American Airlines credit card:.

    Sources indicate that spending on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card could earn you elite status, which I know will interest many. That’s the primary reason you’ll want to consider this card for spending.

    I do want to specifically point out one thing that throws people off — you earn one Loyalty Point per dollar spent on the card, unrelated to how many miles you earn for spending. In other words, if you’re making an American Airlines purchase, you’d earn 4x AAdvantage redeemable miles, but only 1x Loyalty Points on the purchase as such.

    In addition to earning one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can also earn up to 40,000 Loyalty Points every year just for being a cardmember:.

    It has been revealed that in other words, if you have this card, you’d only otherwise need to earn 170,000 Loyalty Points for Executive Platinum status, since this card would get you a boost of 30,000 Loyalty Points at that level. Those Loyalty Points can be earned in a variety of ways, ranging from flying, to online shopping, to credit card spending, to booking vacation packages. Either way, this Loyalty Points boost would be quite the advantage in terms of qualifying for Loyalty Point Rewards, and even upgrade priority.

    In a recent development, the AAdvantage elite qualifying year goes from the beginning of March until the end of February of the following year. You don’t need to have the card at the beginning of the year to take advantage of this, so even if you open the card during the membership year, you could still earn 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points for that year (in other words, the credits can be retroactive).

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has no foreign transaction fees, so this can be a good option for purchases abroad.

    While you’ll want to consult the full cardmember agreement and guide to benefits, the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers useful travel protection, including trip cancellation coverage, trip interruption coverage, trip delay protection, lost baggage protection, rental car coverage, and more.

    So this is a good card to potentially use for travel purchases, since you have to put them on your card to take advantage of those benefits.

    Sources indicate that one of the main reasons you may want to get the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the lounge access perks that the card offers. Having the Citi AA Executive Card is the best way to access Admirals Clubs. Let’s discuss how that works.

    Recent findings suggest that the primary cardmember on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card receives a full Admirals Club membership, including guesting privileges. That in and of itself is a reason this card makes sense.

    While Admirals Clubs aren’t anything to get too excited about, they are improving nicely, in terms of design, and also in terms of the quality of food and beverages. I also appreciate the expansion of the Provisions by Admirals Club concept, whereby the airline offers Admirals Club members grab & go facility, where they can get some drinks or snacks to go before their flight.

    Ordinarily, if you were to buy a comparable Admirals Club membership with guesting privileges, you’d pay a minimum of $1,200 per year.

    By getting an Admirals Club membership with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you’re saving $505-705 right off the bat.

    Note that while you can redeem miles for an Admirals Club membership, it’s a terrible value, as you’re getting only a cent per mile.

    What you get with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a full Admirals Club membership, so you don’t even have to bring your credit card, as your membership will be linked to your AAdvantage number:.

    Admirals Club members don’t get access to Flagship Lounges, as that access is determined based on the ticket you purchased rather than any membership.

    Many people may be considering applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card shortly before taking an American Airlines trip. How soon after being approved for the card does your Admirals Club membership kick in?

    Since the primary cardmember gets a full Admirals Club membership, it’s linked to their AAdvantage account. Many may be surprised to learn that this membership could very well kick in before you even receive your credit card in the mail, and you don’t even need your card to enter a lounge.

    Sources indicate that fortunately, there’s an easy way to tell if your Admirals Club membership has been activated. To figure it out, pretend that you’re signing up for an Admirals Club membership. Go to this page, enter your AAdvantage number, last name, and password.

    If your account has already been updated to reflect the Admirals Club membership, you’ll see that the next page shows “1-Year Citi AADV Exec CC Membership.”.

    If it hasn’t been updated, you’ll see that it gives you the option of choosing what kind of membership you want to purchase.

    Recent findings suggest that note that this only works for the primary cardmember. Since the authorized people don’t get a full Admirals Club membership, they wouldn’t show up as being eligible online. Authorized users need to present the physical Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, since there’s no membership linked to their AAdvantage account.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card also offers Admirals Club access for authorized users. As I explained above, you can add up to three authorized users for a total of $175, which potentially comes out to under $60 per authorized user. I’d say that’s a real sweet spot, since securing lounge access for friends and family for under $60 each is an amazing value.

    Note that authorized customers receive Admirals Club access and not a membership, so there are the restrictions:.

    For the purposes of accessing Admirals Clubs this is more or less the same as an outright membership.

    On the next page, you’ll be able to manage authorized users, including adding and removing them.

    You’ll just need their name to add them, and you have the choice of whether or not you want to give them permission to access your online account.

    Make sure you trust all your authorized customers, since any charges they incur will be your responsibility.

    The primary reason to get the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the great welcome bonus, ability to earn status with spending, ability to receive 40,000 Loyalty Points annually just for being a cardmember, and Admirals Club benefit.

    In a recent development, however, the Citi AA Executive Card offers some other perks that could add a lot of value for card members. These perks range from priority check-in at business class counters, to early boarding, to inflight or Admirals Club credits, to savings with American Airlines Vacations, Lyft, Avis, Budget, Global Entry, or TSA PreCheck, to elite status with Avis and Omni.

    Below is what you need to know about all the other perks of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card.

    Those with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card receive a first checked bag free on domestic American Airlines itineraries not just for themselves, but also for up to eight companions traveling on the same reservation. There’s no need to actually pay for the ticket with your Citi AAdvantage Executive Card — you just have to make sure it’s linked to your AAdvantage account (this benefit applies for the primary cardmember only).

    American ordinarily charges $45-50 for the first checked bag, so that’s a $90-100 value per person roundtrip (and if you had eight companions all checking a bag, that would be a value of $810-900).

    One thing that sometimes throws off cardmembers is that this benefit doesn’t work for international flights, and it doesn’t work for a second bag, if your fare includes one bag. So just understand this is exclusively a first checked bag benefit on domestic flights.

    Industry observers note that for being the primary cardmember on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card you receive several valuable airport benefits, including priority check-in, priority airport screening, and early boarding. These are all features that can save you time and money.

    There’s no need to show your card, as these perks should automatically be reflected with your ticket when you have your credit card linked to your AAdvantage account (which is automatic when you’re the primary cardmember).

    In a recent development, the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $500 in statement credits per calendar year toward American Airlines Vacations purchases. American Airlines Vacations is the carrier’s vacation package portal. This credit is semi-annual, meaning you can take advantage of a $250 credit every six months (once in January through June, and once in July through December).

    Sources indicate that this applies for a booking of two or more travel components, like a flight, car reservation, or hotel booking. Many people find American Airlines Vacations to be a great deal, and a good way to earn bonus Loyalty Points.

    It has been revealed that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $200 in InKind credits every year. This comes in the form of a $100 semi-annual credit, with one being available January 1 through June 30, and the other being available July 1 through December 31. This can be used across multiple meals, and tips aren’t covered by the credit. Either the primary cardmember or authorized users can use the perk, though authorized users don’t get extra credits.

    InKind is my favorite dining rewards app, and to me, this is basically good as cash. I dine at InKind restaurants constantly, as there are some really high quality restaurants on the list, so I value this new card perk immensely. If you’re new to InKind, make sure you also register through a refer-a-friend link, so you can get an extra credit.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $180 in Lyft credits every year. This comes in the form of a $15 Lyft credit each month after taking three eligible rides. The Lyft credit expires 30 days after it’s issued. Either the primary cardmember or authorized consumers can use the perk, though authorized users don’t get extra credits. Admittedly this requires quite a bit of effort to use, so not everyone will get value from that.

    Recent findings suggest that just for having the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can receive up to $120 back on eligible Avis or Budget rentals every calendar year. Just charge an eligible pre-paid rental to your card each year, and you’ll receive a statement credit up to the $120 limit. This can be used toward a single rental or multiple rentals made directly with Avis or Budget. If you rent with Avis and Budget with any frequency, this could be worth face value.

    Just for having the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can receive up to $100 in statement credits every calendar year toward spending onboard American flights, or in Admirals Clubs. So you can use this credit to purchase everything from premium drinks or snacks on flights, to premium alcoholic drinks in Admirals Clubs.

    Just charge the eligible purchase to your card, and you’ll be reimbursed automatically, with no registration required.

    Recent findings suggest that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit once every four years, which is worth up to $120. Simply charge the purchase to your card and it will automatically be reimbursed. You don’t have to be the one signing up — you can always pay for a friend or family member who is signing up instead.

    Personally, I always recommend applying for Global Entry, because Global Entry automatically comes with TSA PreCheck, while the inverse isn’t true.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card now offers some perks with Omni Hotels & Resorts. For those not familiar, Omni operates around 50 properties in the United States and Canada, so there’s value in getting extra perks at these hotels. Specifically:.

    It has been revealed that to take advantage of this, you’ll want to enroll before your stay, book your stay direct with Omni, and pay with the card. If you stay at Omni properties with any frequencies, this is quite a nice value-add, if you ask me.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers complimentary Avis President’s Club status, with enrollment available through August 31, 2028.

    Recent findings suggest that avis President’s Club status offers a variety of perks, including car upgrades, expedited service, complimentary additional drivers, and more. If you rent from Avis, you should definitely be able to get some value from this.

    In a recent development, the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a World Legend Mastercard, meaning that it comes with quite a few benefits you may not be familiar with. In addition to the concierge service, there are also savings and other perks with a variety of businesses, ranging from DoorDash to HelloFresh.

    Let me once again state that this card used to be known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard, before recently being rebranded as a World Legend Mastercard.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a lucrative card that I personally have and also recommend, but only if you’re a frequent flyer with American. If you fly American with any frequency then an Admirals Club membership is valuable, and this is the best way to get an Admirals Club membership. There can even be value in adding up to three authorized people, which will cost a total of $175, as they’d get Admirals Club access as well.

    In addition to lounge access, the Citi AA Executive Card offers up to 40,000 Loyalty Points per year (even without spending money on the card), which can make a substantial difference for anyone chasing status with American. Furthermore, the card potentially offers hundreds of dollars in credits per year, which can help offset the annual fee.

    However, this isn’t a card that I’d use for my everyday spending unless I specifically valued the added Loyalty Points from spending. Otherwise, there are much more rewarding cards for everyday spending, and I’d just hold onto this card for the very strong perks, including lounge access, and the bonus Loyalty Points without a spending requirement.

    For my mental accounting purposes, I take the $695 annual fee, and then subtract the $200 InKind credit, which I consider to basically be worth face value. That really takes the “out of pocket” on the card to $495 per year for me, which is an amazing deal for the Admirals Club membership and bonus Loyalty Points.

    While the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is American’s most premium credit card, it’s also worth being aware of the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® (learn more), which has a $350 annual fee. There are lots of reasons to consider that card, including an excellent welcome bonus. Among other things:.

    I think there’s potentially merit to having both cards, especially if you value earning the Loyalty Points bonuses. Otherwise I’d say the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is easier to justify if you’re an occasional American flyer, while I think the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is easier to justify if you value an Admirals Club membership.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card isn’t for everyone. If you’re not a frequent flyer on American then you shouldn’t consider this card. However, if you are a frequent flyer on American then this card is totally for you.

    While Admirals Clubs aren’t anything to get too excited about, there’s still huge value in the complimentary snacks and drinks, free Wi-Fi and quiet places to sit, and access to an agent in the event your flight has irregular operations.

    Even beyond the Admirals Club membership, the card offers other useful perks, like the ability to earn Loyalty Points, priority services with American, and the ability to receive credits with American Airlines Vacations, InKind, Avis, Budget, Lyft, and more.

    In a recent development, I’ve had the Citi AA Executive Card for years, and love it. If you don’t yet have the card, this is a good time to apply, given the offer that’s available.

    If you want to learn more about the Citi Executive AAdvantage Card or want to apply, follow this link.

    Ryanair Now Withholds Free Seats Until Just Before Departure, Blames Customer Feedback

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, ryanair has quietly updated its policy for how it assigns seats to those people who don’t pay the seat assignment fee, as reported by The Irish Times.
    • Ryanair is known for being an unapologetic ultra low cost carrier.
    • It has been revealed that however, the way the airline is randomly allocating seats has quietly changed as of late October 2026, coinciding with the start of the winter schedule.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, ryanair has quietly updated its policy for how it assigns seats to those people who don’t pay the seat assignment fee, as reported by The Irish Times. While I wouldn’t consider this to be anything unreasonable, what I’m amused by is the carrier’s justification. The airline claims that it’s doing this due to customer feedback, rather than to generate more revenue.

    Ryanair is known for being an unapologetic ultra low cost carrier. The airline has low base fares, and then charges fees for just about everything. Among other things, the airline charges to assign seats in advance, and those who don’t pay for specific seat assignments are just randomly assigned seats (and often in a rather punitive way).

    It has been revealed that however, the way the airline is randomly allocating seats has quietly changed as of late October 2026, coinciding with the start of the winter schedule. Historically, the airline has automatically assigned seats to passengers without seat assignments around 24 hours before departure.

    Some passengers seemed to “game” this, and would essentially “gamble.” What they’d do is wait until 24 hours out to see what seat they were assigned for free. Then if they weren’t happy with their automatic seat assignment, they could still pay to assign a better seat.

    Sources indicate that under the latest policy, the airline still problems a boarding pass up to 24 hours out, but without a seat assignment. Then the boarding pass automatically indicates the seat assignment within four hours of departure.

    According to recent reports, the logic here seems pretty clear — some people do care somewhat about where they sit, but want to avoid fees if they can. By withholding seat assignments until hours before departure, passengers are presumably more likely to pay for seat assignments in advance, to avoid that uncertainty.

    Ryanair has confirmed this seat assignment policy change in a statement, sharing that “the timing of the allocation of free random seats is determined at all times by the airline.” Right, nobody disputes that the airline has the right to do this.

    So, what’s the logic for this policy change? According to the airline, it’s “to allow those passengers who wish to select their preferred seat more time to do so. We had a number of complaints this summer that passengers could not book their preferred seat on the day of travel as it had been already randomly allocated as a free seat up to 24 hours prior to departure.”.

    The Ryanair representative went on to say that “passengers who choose a free of charge random seat clearly don’t mind where they sit, and their digital boarding pass is automatically updated between three to four hours prior to departure, which is well before they arrive at either their departure airport or their boarding gate.”.

    Ryanair is of course within its rights to have this policy, but I think the logic is pretty obvious, and it’s to generate more revenue. After all, 24 hours out people would see what they were randomly assigned at online check-in, and would still have a lot of choices if they wanted to pay for seats, since most people don’t check-in online exactly at the 24-hour mark.

    But within a few hours of departure, virtually everyone has checked in online, and not many seats will be left. So I imagine the goal is to condition more customers to pay for seat assignments in advance. I love the claim that customers complained that their preferred seats on the day of travel were randomly allocated to others for free:.

    Ryanair has a new policy for automatic seat allocations. In the past, the airline would automatically assign seats to passengers 24 hours out, giving them quite the window to “gamble” on the free seat assignment, and then pay for a different seat assignment if they weren’t happy with the free one.

    The airline has now started only assigning free seats at most four hours out. The airline claims that this is due to customer feedback, so that passengers have more time to assign their choice of paid seats. However, I imagine that’s not quite accurate, and this is instead about conditioning people to pay for seat assignments, rather than “gambling” on the free allocations.

    What do you make of this Ryanair seating policy change?

    Breaking: Iran resolution blocked in first war powers vote since midterms

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tim Kaine, D-Va., seen here at the Capitol on June 17, remarked additional war powers votes are under discussion for when Democrats control both chambers in the 120th Congress.
    • The Senate rejected a resolution Thursday meant to rebuke President Donald Trump over the Iran war weeks after the midterm elections demonstrated the depth of public anger about the war and its effects on the U.S.
    • Industry observers note that senators voted 48-51 against adopting the Iran war powers resolution that the House previously adopted in mid-September that would direct the president to withdraw U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., seen here at the Capitol on June 17, remarked additional war powers votes are under discussion for when Democrats control both chambers in the 120th Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    The Senate rejected a resolution Thursday meant to rebuke President Donald Trump over the Iran war weeks after the midterm elections demonstrated the depth of public anger about the war and its effects on the U.S. economy.

    Industry observers note that senators voted 48-51 against adopting the Iran war powers resolution that the House previously adopted in mid-September that would direct the president to withdraw U.S. forces from the war.

    It has been revealed that as they have previously with similar measures, GOP Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky broke with their party to support the resolution, while Democratic Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania broke with his party to oppose it. Departing GOP Sens. Thom Tillis of North Carolina and Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, who have at times voted in support of similar measures, this time voted against the resolution.

    Even if the resolution was adopted in both chambers of Congress, it would be largely symbolic since, as a concurrent resolution, it would not go to the president for his signature.

    But the vote afforded senators the opportunity to register their complaints about the war for the first time since Democrats routed Republicans in the midterm elections.

    It also comes amid a larger debate within the Democratic Party on how best to fulfill their campaign promise of ending the war as they prepare to take control of Congress next year.

    Democrats have become increasingly interested in trying to cut off funding for the war rather than continuing to hold war powers votes. But they are divided on whether to demand an immediate end to funding in the next government funding bill in December or to wait until they take power in January.

    “When we have the gavels, we are contemplating other things, and we're actually contemplating things in connection with the CR discussion,” Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., told reporters Thursday in an apparent reference to the debate among Democrats.

    According to recent reports, as of Nov. 13, the war has cost at least $48.3 billion, up from $47 billion last month, the nominee to be Navy comptroller, Arthur Miller, told the Senate Armed Services Committee at his confirmation hearing Thursday.

    As with previous estimates, the number Miller cited Thursday includes munitions, equipment replacement costs and operational costs but does not factor in the cost of damage to U.S. bases, which alone is likely to run in the billions.

    Recent findings suggest that last week, a trio of Senate Democrats unveiled legislation to prohibit funding for offensive military operations in Iran that they stated they intend to introduce as an amendment to the next government funding bill, which Congress will need to pass to avoid a government shutdown after Dec. 11.

    In a recent development, on Thursday as the Senate voted on the war powers resolution, Sens. Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., and Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., two of the sponsors of the proposed amendment, demanded it be included in the next funding bill.

    “We’ve already tried tool after tool to get the president to rein in this conflict. Nine months in, defunding the war is the only way to force Trump to end it,” Duckworth, who vowed to vote against any continuing resolution that doesn’t include the amendment, said at a news conference.

    It has been revealed that sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., unveiled his own proposed amendment Thursday to bar any future and previous funding from being used to “support directly or indirectly combat activities by United States personnel in or over Iran, or in Iranian territorial waters” unless specifically authorized by Congress.

    His legislation is modeled off of language Congress passed in 1973 to cut off funding for the Nixon administration’s bombing campaign in Cambodia, Bennet’s office said in a news release.

    Industry observers note that “When we vote on short-term spending in the near future, we can fund the government and end this war. It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve,” Bennet mentioned in a statement.

    Meanwhile, the House is likely to vote again on a war powers resolution before year’s end.

    Sources indicate that “Before the lame duck’s over, I hope to enforce a war powers resolution vote, and it’ll be a chance for Republicans to say whether they did or didn’t get the message on Nov. 3,” Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., remarked Thursday in a brief interview, referring to the date of the elections.

    Industry observers note that as with previous resolutions, Massie’s would direct the president to remove U.S. military units from hostilities against Iran unless specifically authorized by Congress or needed to defend against an imminent attack.

    Sources indicate that the resolution was filed Nov. 10, and under the 1973 War Powers Resolution, Massie can force a vote 15 calendar days after its introduction.

    John M. Donnelly and Lauren Green contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, on November 17, 2026, Uzbekistan's civil aviation authority granted Luxembourg-based Cargolux Airlines a permit to operate scheduled cargo flights to Navoi International Airport (NVI) with Boeing 747F freighters. The surprise is that a major widebody cargo carrier, operating a 30-aircraft fleet of Boeing 747-400Fs and 747-8Fs, is betting on Navoi as a pure-play cargo hub with a free customs zone as opposed to focusing on Tashkent, the Uzbek capital.

    Industry observers note that for most travelers, Navoi barely registers on the aviation map, but freight planners are looking closely at what the airport offers. Why would one of the world's largest cargo airlines pursue regulatory approval for a small Central Asian airport before announcing a launch date, frequency, routing, payload, or European network link? For Cargolux, opting for an airport out of the spotlight may just be one of the best moves available.

    Uzbekistan's civil aviation regulator, the Uzaviation Agency, granted Cargolux Airlines a permit to operate scheduled Boeing 747F cargo services to Navoi International Airport, setting the scene for one of the more intriguing route expansions. The authorization builds on earlier bilateral aviation ties, including a 2019 air traffic protocol designed to support Cargolux transit cargo flows to Asian markets starting in 2020.

    An important shift in how Navoi is governed helps explain why the hub is drawing direct freighter interest now. Navoi International Airport was decoupled from centralized operational control under Uzbekistan Airports LLC in 2026, gaining commercial autonomy to negotiate agreements directly with international airlines and logistics partners, as reported by the Tashkent Times.

    It has been revealed that operating independently lets Navoi tailor slot coordination, ground arrangements, and commercial terms to cargo operators rather than competing for attention inside a passenger-led airport group. Navoi reinforced that cargo-first positioning in October 2026 with the opening of its Porto-Franco free customs zone, established under Presidential Resolution No. PP-50 of February 9, 2026.

    Described as Central Asia's first free customs zone of its kind, Porto-Franco supports duty-free storage and processing of international goods alongside upgraded ground handling equipment. Together, commercial autonomy and customs-free handling give Navoi a distinct institutional foundation as a dedicated freight hub.

    It has been revealed that uzbekistan's air cargo market has expanded rapidly, creating a strong commercial backdrop for Navoi's push. Air cargo volume in Uzbekistan climbed 182% between 2019 and 2024 before rising another 33% in the first half of 2026, per Trend News Agency. That sustained growth reflects rising trade flows across Central Asia and growing demand for reliable transit links between Asia and Europe.

    Geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East have added urgency to that shift by straining traditional southern routing options. As conflict-related closures and airspace restrictions affect Gulf hubs and Middle Eastern corridors, freight forwarders and airlines have increasingly looked toward Central Asian transit routes as an alternative connection point between Asian manufacturing centers and European markets.

    Sources indicate that uzbekistan sits directly along that overland and aerial corridor, making it an ideal location under these circumstances. Within Uzbekistan, Navoi is being positioned as a dedicated cargo and multimodal logistics hub and is not necessarily competing head-to-head with Tashkent's passenger-heavy gateway.

    It has been revealed that connecting air freighters with regional rail and road networks allows shipments to move smoothly across Eurasia and keeps heavy freighter traffic away from crowded capital-city passenger operations. For cargo operators, that separation makes Navoi a cleaner fit for high-volume transit.

    Backing up Navoi's hub ambitions can only be achieved with improved capacity on the ground as freighter traffic scales up, as detailed in reporting from Air Cargo Week. That capacity is well on its way, with a upcoming 172,223-square-foot (16,000-square-meter) cargo terminal under construction at the airport, paired with fuel storage expanded to 16,535 short tons (15,000 metric tons) to support long-range widebody turnarounds.

    Those upgrades give cargo operators dedicated warehouse space and reliable uplift in a way that does not strain existing apron operations. Technical and maintenance support is also part of the buildout roadmap as Navoi prepares for heavier widebody use. According to Trend News Agency, prepares include a dedicated aircraft maintenance and painting center for widebody aircraft targeted for completion by 2028.

    This will expand local technical capabilities alongside cargo handling. Ultimately, having heavy maintenance and paint capacity closer to the corridor reduces repositioning overhead for operators. Those investments tie directly to ambitious operational targets set for the end of the decade, highlighted in coverage by UzDaily and Trend News Agency.

    According to recent reports, navoi is aiming for 7,000 annual flights and 49,604 short tons (45,000 metric tons) of cargo by 2030 as commercial agreements and logistics partnerships scale up. Hitting those milestones, though, will all depend on the planned terminals, fuel capacity, and 2028 maintenance facilities and whether these can provide steady daily throughput.

    Sources indicate that cargolux brings a specialized all-cargo fleet built around the 747 family, with a 30-aircraft lineup of Boeing 747-400F and 747-8F freighters detailed in Trans.ru's report on the permit and Cargolux's fleet overview. What makes the 747 particularly unique and well-suited to cargo operations is its nose-loading capability.

    Nose-loading widebody freighters are well suited to bulky, outsized, and high-value shipments moving along Eurasian corridors where straight-in main-deck loading saves handling time and supports long-range trunk lift. Even with the November 17, 2026 approval in hand, key operational details remain unannounced within UzDaily's coverage of the permit and Kapital.uz's report.

    In a recent development, neither a launch date nor flight frequency has been disclosed, and public reporting has not yet confirmed exact routings, payload allocations, or how Navoi flights will link into Cargolux's broader European network out of Luxembourg. From the viewpoint of cargo planners and shippers, that gap means the permit marks a regulatory green light rather than an immediate timetable.

    Until schedules and routing structures are published, market watchers will look to subsequent announcements, whether that be from media outlets or the airline itself, to see whether Navoi will be a dedicated regional stop, a multi-sector transit point, or an overflow hub for high-density freight.

    In a recent development, navoi's pure-play cargo and multimodal positioning sets it apart from Tashkent as well as other Central Asian and nearby Caucasus logistics hubs competing for Asia–Europe freight, as examined by Air Cargo Week and Seetao. Other airports in the region generally rely on belly hold capacity tied to passenger schedules.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Navoi focuses on dedicated freighter turnarounds backed by road and rail links across Central Asia and China–Europe trade lanes. Across the wider region, airports and logistics corridors in Central Asia and the Caucasus are expanding capacity simultaneously to capture shifting transit flows, as covered in Air Cargo Week's regional cargo capacity analysis.

    According to recent reports, competition centers on customs efficiency, ground handling speed, and seamless links between air corridors and overland rail or trucking routes. Airports such as Baku Heydar Aliyev Airport (GYD) already have established cargo demand, supported by Baku-based Silk Way West as well as the presence of operators such as Cargolux. Overall, Navoi is looking to be in a really good position to establish itself strongly in the global cargo network.

    As such, it may not be long before more operators, in addition to Cargolux, look to cement their operations in this Central Asian hub. Regional hub rivalry comes down to execution and reliability, and Navoi's infrastructure growth epitomizes this. Hubs that pair multimodal connectivity with predictable clearance and turnaround times stand the best chance of holding onto Asia–Europe cargo once routing choices stabilize.

    Cargolux's November 17, 2026 permit to operate Boeing 747F flights to Navoi International Airport is a major milestone for Central Asian aviation, a decision that highlights how shifting trade corridors, Middle East airspace disruptions, and hub design are reshaping Asia–Europe air cargo.

    Industry observers note that with commercial autonomy and the Porto-Franco free customs zone, alongside a 30-aircraft 747-400F and 747-8F operator, Navoi has an incredible opening to compete as a dedicated freighter hub rather than an afterthought behind Tashkent. Going from regulatory approval to sustained commercial volume will depend on decision-making across both airlines and airport planners over the coming years.

    While launch dates, frequencies, routings, payloads, and European network ties remain unannounced, Navoi's 172,223-square-foot (16,000-square-meter) cargo terminal buildout, 16,535-short-ton (15,000-metric-ton) fuel storage expansion, 2028 widebody maintenance and painting center, and 2030 goals of 7,000 annual flights and 49,604 short tons (45,000 metric tons) of cargo set clear benchmarks.

    Recent findings suggest that ultimately, whether Navoi becomes a permanent fixture on Cargolux's 747 map will come down to real-world performance when up against rival hubs across Central Asia and the Caucasus. If multimodal rail and road links, customs clearance, and widebody ground support deliver consistent turnarounds as traffic grows, an airport most flyers have never heard of could support a major link in Eurasian cargo logistics.

    Latest Update: Mobile Passport Control: Free App That Speeds Up US Immigration

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1478 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, frequent travelers to the United States are probably familiar with Global Entry, which allows enrolled members to get expedited immigration at US airports.
    • Sources indicate that if you don’t want Global Entry (or aren’t eligible), your next best option is Mobile Passport Control.
    • Mobile Passport Control (MPC) is a free app that allows travelers to submit their travel document, photo, and customs declaration information, before they arrive at the immigration checkpoint at a US airport.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, frequent travelers to the United States are probably familiar with Global Entry, which allows enrolled members to get expedited immigration at US airports. However, applying for Global Entry is a bit of a process, and there’s a cost to participate.

    Sources indicate that if you don’t want Global Entry (or aren’t eligible), your next best option is Mobile Passport Control. This is sort of a hidden program that doesn’t get talked about enough, given that it can significantly cut down your wait times at US immigration. In this post, I’d like to talk about how this works, as I’ve used it a couple of times now (when traveling internationally with our younger son, who doesn’t yet have Global Entry).

    Mobile Passport Control (MPC) is a free app that allows travelers to submit their travel document, photo, and customs declaration information, before they arrive at the immigration checkpoint at a US airport.

    Travelers just have to download the app, which is available for Apple and Android. The idea is that the app streamlines the traveler’s entry process to the United States by reducing passport control inspection times and overall wait times.

    Sources indicate that those who use MPC can access a separate immigration screening checkpoint. Really that’s the biggest advantage — because not many people use this program (as of now), the wait times are generally much shorter than the standard wait times.

    There are some key things to be aware of, as you’d expect:.

    In the interest of being thorough, here are the current airports participating in Mobile Passport Control:.

    Sources indicate that the Mobile Passport Control app couldn’t be much easier to use. I’d recommend downloading the app prior to boarding your flight to the United States, and completing the basic requirements. Then you have to submit your customs declaration after you land in the United States (within four hours of when you intend to clear immigration).

    Once you download the app, there are several pages explaining how the app works, plus you have to agree to a disclaimer statement.

    After that you can go through steps required for a particular entry to the country. Note that you can use one app to submit your application for multiple people in the same family. Furthermore, you can save the passport details in the app for multiple trips, eliminating the need to submit all of this information each time (though you do need to make a customs declaration each time).

    To start the process, you’ll have to state which CBP port you’ll be arriving at, and they all show on a dropdown menu.

    According to recent reports, at that point you’ll have to select the travelers who will be entering the country. If you’ve already saved people to your profile, they’ll show on that page. Otherwise you can start from scratch, which just requires scanning the document, and then all the information will be auto-populated.

    You’ll then need to capture traveler photos. This doesn’t need to be a passport-quality photo — you just have to follow some very basic guidelines, like removing hats and sunglasses, and making sure only one person’s face is visible.

    It has been revealed that the above can all be saved to your profile. However, what you do need to complete with each trip is answering six standard CBP declaration questions.

    Industry observers note that you’ll only want to submit this when you arrive at your point of entry in the United States. The app asks you to submit this once you’ve arrived at the airport, though in reality you have up to four hours to go through immigration from the time that your application is submitted.

    Once you submit your document, you’ll be given a receipt with a QR code, which you’ll need to scan when you see an immigration officer.

    Once you land at your US point of entry and arrive in the immigration hall, look for the Mobile Passport Control signage. This will bring you to an area separate from the standard US immigration line.

    According to recent reports, you still need to queue to see an immigration officer, and when you get to the officer, you’ll see a scanning device where you should scan your QR code. The benefit is that this line is usually much shorter, and also that you generally won’t be asked as many questions (since you’ve already answered some questions via the app).

    Sources indicate that both times I’ve gone through the MPC lane, the wait was less than five minutes, while the general immigration line looked much longer. The main benefit of MPC isn’t even the time savings from getting some of the work done in advance through the app, but rather just having access to a shorter line.

    Recent findings suggest that mobile Passport Control isn’t as good as Global Entry, plain and simple. With Global Entry there’s almost never a wait, you just have to look at the camera, an officer acknowledges you, and then you’re usually sent on your way. The Mobile Passport Control experience isn’t as seamless. However, it’s the next best thing.

    Sources indicate that there’s no enrollment cost, using the app takes maybe a few minutes to set up, and then with each trip it just takes a minute or so to answer the declaration questions. Getting access to a special immigration line for that is awesome, as it could potentially save you a significant amount of time.

    Of course like many things in life, I imagine that as this app becomes more popular and well known, it will also become less useful. After all, when everyone gets access to a special lane, no one gets access to a special lane. 😉.

    Industry observers note that mobile Passport Control is an awesome free app that can save you time at US immigration. The app is easy to use, and allows you to submit your documents and customs declaration prior to speaking to an immigration officer. Most valuable of all, those with MPC get access to a special lane at immigration, which is typically much shorter than the standard one.

    While I’d still recommend Global Entry, those who don’t have it should use MPC if they’re eligible.

    • Kyle Balzer is a resident fellow at the American Enterprise Institute where he specializes in nuclear strategy and policy.

    President Trump left his Shenzhen summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin last week still dreaming of a denuclearization agreement with his great-power counterparts. But Trump’s long-held ambition to achieve the deep reductions in nuclear weaponry that Ronald Reagan secured with his Soviet counterpart Mikhail Gorbachev in the 1980s clashes with reality. Chinese and Russian officials may now be speaking the language of “strategic stability,” but Trump would be wise to recognize that these pronouncements are intended to deter him from taking the steps necessary to strengthen America’s nuclear deterrence.

    Unlike Gorbachev in the final years of the Cold War, neither Xi nor Putin presently has any appetite for meaningful arms-control negotiations. Xi acts as if his geopolitical position compares favorably with America’s. Both men are wielding their nuclear power to weaken America’s security and dissolve its alliances. Consider Putin’s nuclear threats during the war in Ukraine and Xi’s campaign of coercion in the western Pacific, which is shielded by China’s growing nuclear arsenal.

    Kyle Balzer is a resident fellow at the American Enterprise Institute where he specializes in nuclear strategy and policy.

    Sources indicate that it’s a well-established gambit. A politician starts criticizing Jews. He gains followers. His attacks grow, along with his political power.

    Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen (D.), who is challenging Chuck Schumer for the position of Senate majority leader, is adopting this playbook. Van Hollen, who alleged in a recent Fresh York Times op-ed that Israelis have “increasingly undermined American interests and values,” has become one of the foremost critics of the Jewish state in Congress. Backed by progressives such as Bernie Sanders, he is basking in his newfound fame. His foray into the Senate leadership contest coincided with his push to strip provisions concerning U.S. security cooperation with Israel from the National Defense Authorization Act. These and other broadsides have made him a darling of the anti-Zionist left. Regardless of whether he supplants Schumer, Van Hollen is pushing the Senate ever leftward on its policy toward Israel.

    Recent findings suggest that daniel J. Samet is a Jeane Kirkpatrick Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute. He interned for then-Representative Van Hollen in 2015.

    #157201. Van Hollen: Senate rules changes a matter for caucus to decide

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (553 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Van Hollen: Senate rules changes a matter for caucus to decide

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., during a press conference on Thursday.
    • Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., endorsed a bipartisan plan Thursday to adopt latest rules aimed at speeding up Senate procedures but stopped short of calling for abolishing the filibuster, laying down a marker on a key internal debate for Democrats as he positions himself to challenge Senate Minority Leader Charles E.
    • Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., at a press conference Thursday to express his support for a strategy from Merkley and Sen.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore. looks on as Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., during a press conference on Thursday. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images).

    Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., endorsed a bipartisan plan Thursday to adopt latest rules aimed at speeding up Senate procedures but stopped short of calling for abolishing the filibuster, laying down a marker on a key internal debate for Democrats as he positions himself to challenge Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y.

    Van Hollen joined Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., at a press conference Thursday to express his support for a strategy from Merkley and Sen. Steve Daines, R-Mont., to, among other changes, adopt a “talking filibuster,” requiring senators to continuously hold the floor if they seek to prevent a bill or nomination from moving forward.

    Van Hollen went further to say that while his personal view is that the filibuster itself is “anti-democratic,” changes beyond what Merkley and Daines are proposing are a matter for further discussion.

    It has been revealed that “I’m in favor of filibuster reform,” Van Hollen said. “How and when we do that is a matter for the caucus to decide.”.

    The filibuster, a Senate tactic that effectively requires a 60-vote threshold to advance most legislation, has long been the subject of calls for change or outright abolition from members of both parties.

    Other changes Merkley and Daines unveiled in October include eliminating cloture requirements for nominations and amendments, reducing post-cloture time for legislation, and introducing a upcoming suspension process modeled after the House rules to allow bills with broad support to move rapidly.

    Merkley actually held two separate press conferences Thursday on his filibuster proposal, one with his Montana Republican co-sponsor and then later with Van Hollen, whose bid to become majority leader he has endorsed.

    At the earlier appearance, Daines stated that he thought the changes, if adopted, would “truly be a cultural change for the Senate” and lead to greater bipartisanship.

    “We believe these reforms are appropriate no matter who is in the majority, no matter what the election outcomes were,” Daines stated.

    Daines also reiterated his view that implementing any rules changes would require 67 votes from the full chamber.

    But Democrats have been debating whether to use their new majority in 2027 to change the rules on the first day of the session with 51 votes, or to eventually employ the so-called “nuclear option,” a series of procedural moves leading to a simple majority vote.

    Democrats used that tool in 2013 to lower the voting threshold for advancing some presidential nominations with a simple majority, rather than 60 votes. A Republican majority followed in 2017 by extending that change to include Supreme Court nominations, and again in 2019 to reduce the number of hours between a cloture and final confirmation vote.

    A spokesperson for Schumer declined to comment on Van Hollen’s endorsement of the Merkley-Daines proposal.

    Schumer has stated he remains confident in his bid to remain party leader.

    Van Hollen reiterated Thursday that his “momentum is growing,” after several senators-elect have thrown their support behind the Maryland Democrat.

    “I think people recognize that if we're going to deliver on the big things that the American voters stood up for and voted for, you can't just go back to business as usual and status quo,” Van Hollen remarked.

    #157199. Your Flight Takes 10 Minutes Longer Than It Used To—And That’s A Luxury Worth Paying For

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2229 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Your Flight Takes 10 Minutes Longer Than It Used To—And That’s A Luxury Worth Paying For

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2229 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Flying takes longer than it used to – and, retirement of the Concorde notwithstanding, it’s not because planes aren’t as fast.
    • By one estimate flights have gotten 8% longer.
    • Airlines are often chided for ‘schedule padding’ – claiming that flights take longer than they should.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Flying takes longer than it used to – and, retirement of the Concorde notwithstanding, it’s not because planes aren’t as fast. There are more than twice as many commercial flights as there were at the time of airline deregulation, and air traffic control hasn’t been upgraded very much. There’s congested airspace and also congested airports. We also don’t build major upcoming airports – the last one was Denver, 30 years ago. (Austin’s new 1999 airport was a converted military base, and there were others like that in the 90s.) By one estimate flights have gotten 8% longer. That means a two hour flight is 10 minutes longer than it used to be. And the single biggest factor is often tagged as strategic padding of schedules. Airlines are often chided for ‘schedule padding’ – claiming that flights take longer than they should. Often, this just reflects the reality of telling customers when they can expect to arrive – although there’s greater variance than there used to be, which isn’t great for having a gate available when you land early. Airlines do not like this! Though real airfares (even including fees) are down significantly since deregulation, longer flight times are expensive for staffing, fuel and efficient use of $50 – $100 million planes. And longer travel times historically disadvantaged an airline trying to sell tickets, because it meant their flights were displayed lower on the screen that travel agents and later passengers directly saw – which translates into fewer sales. A new study finds that airlines with more “padding” in their schedules tend to charge higher fares. That sounds like passengers paying more for a slower trip. But those extra minutes can also let United hold your plane with ConnectionSaver and get you home that night, and still arrive on time. It also means fewer delays and missed connections. So that ‘premium’ is actually a more valuable product to many consumers. I’ve argued for years that schedule padding often isn’t really padding. Sometimes an airline is finally admitting how long the trip takes. Customers can proposal around an honest arrival time. There’s a new chapter by Embry-Riddle’s Jules Yimga, “The Price of Punctuality,” in The Economics of Airline Pricing. It combines 2019 flight time data with the government’s ticket price survey. It compares schedules against different percentiles of actual flight times, then examines how the resulting measures relate to fares. More padding is associated with higher fares, especially when the comparison uses the faster end of actual flight times. The relationship appears in both competitive and concentrated markets. The abstract itself allows that reliability could be a service customers value. (Interestingly, Yimga’s earlier research on schedule padding attributed higher prices primarily to higher costs rather than higher margins.) Even scheduling to the median arrival time means roughly half of trips take longer than published. It’s often better for a customer if an airline underpromises and overdelivers – or arrives ‘on time’ rather than late. Predictability matters when you’re scheduling connections or trying to arrive in time for a meeting. An airline that leaves little buffer is going to appear less reliable, so customers book earlier flights and longer layovers or even fly in the night before an crucial meeting. Then the buffer hasn’t disappeared, it just changes who’s scheduling it. That’s why I argued American’s investment in more realistic schedules could pay for itself. Avoiding rebooking, mishandled bags and aircraft and crews getting out of position can justify spending running an on-time schedule even before a customer chooses the airline again because the trip met expectations. American’s Dallas – Fort Worth overhaul that began in April combined longer scheduled flight times with a move from nine daily banks of flights to thirteen. Spreading flights into smaller waves reduced congestion that made some of the extra time unnecessary. One plane waiting for a gate can delay its passengers, its next departure, and other flights whose crews are stuck on board. Giving the operation room to recover can prevent that problem from cascading. In January, I covered American network planning chief Brian Znotins explaining that bookings for 40–54 minute connections at DFW were 4% below what its model predicted. Bookings for 55–84 minute connections were 8% above prediction. Customers have actually started choosing longer connections because they feel more reliable and less likely to leave them stranded. When I covered United’s media day in 2019, Greg Hart explained that 25% of its flights each day were expected to arrive ten minutes early. That gave United room to use ConnectionSaver to hold flights for connecting passengers and still arrive on time. Of course there’s such a thing as too much slack. An airline can improve its reported punctuality by moving the promised arrival later without getting anyone anywhere sooner. Excessively long connections waste customer time. And routinely beating an absurdly generous schedule doesn’t make an operation excellent. Not all padding is something customers will pay a premium for.     • Sources indicate that hilton Honors will give you 2,000 bonus points per stay if you book by Tuesday, December 1.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that hilton Honors will give you 2,000 bonus points per stay if you book by Tuesday, December 1. I value Hilton points at 0.4 cents apiece. That’s $8 for a night at a Hampton Inn or $8 for a week at a Conrad. Book directly with Hilton. The booking window opened November 24, 2026, for stays completed November 25, 2026 through April 2, 2027. There’s no registration required or cap. (Hat tip to Head for Points.)     📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, every year, corporate shareholders have several hundred proposals to vote on at corporate annual meetings or, more often, via their proxy ballots.
    • According to recent reports, unlike many federal rule changes, which often include relatively minor tweaks to the existing bureaucracy, the SEC’s current proposal would repeal a major regulation known as Rule 14a-8 that’s been on the books for decades.
    • Richard Morrison is the host of the Free the Economy podcast and a senior fellow at the Competitive Enterprise Institute.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, every year, corporate shareholders have several hundred proposals to vote on at corporate annual meetings or, more often, via their proxy ballots. Those proposals have become more controversial and divisive over time. The last several years of battles over “woke capitalism” and its inevitable backlash were largely fought through the shareholder resolution process. Now the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is about to rewrite the rules for what makes it onto those shareholder ballots, and that could mean a reset for how politics impacts corporate America — and vice versa.

    According to recent reports, unlike many federal rule changes, which often include relatively minor tweaks to the existing bureaucracy, the SEC’s current proposal would repeal a major regulation known as Rule 14a-8 that’s been on the books for decades. Originally implemented in 1942 and amended multiple times since, the rule gave the SEC the power to referee which ideas corporate boards need to put up for a vote and which ones they can safely ignore. But the SEC is now proposing to repeal the rule entirely, leaving those decisions up to state governments and individual companies.

    Richard Morrison is the host of the Free the Economy podcast and a senior fellow at the Competitive Enterprise Institute.

    Alec Mena is a research fellow at the Competitive Enterprise Institute.

    On “SEC Proposes Reforms to Shareholder Democracy”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that eric Ueland, nominee to be comptroller general, sits at the witness table for his confirmation hearing with the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Thursday.
    • Eric Ueland, President Donald Trump’s pick for comptroller general, promised to be independent and impartial if confirmed, amid criticism from Democrats and outside groups, during a confirmation hearing Thursday.
    • “I’m not here as a plant, a stooge, a lackey for anybody,” he told Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., after Democrats on the panel accused him of being a “rubber stamp” for the administration.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that eric Ueland, nominee to be comptroller general, sits at the witness table for his confirmation hearing with the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Thursday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Eric Ueland, President Donald Trump’s pick for comptroller general, promised to be independent and impartial if confirmed, amid criticism from Democrats and outside groups, during a confirmation hearing Thursday.

    “I’m not here as a plant, a stooge, a lackey for anybody,” he told Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., after Democrats on the panel accused him of being a “rubber stamp” for the administration.

    It has been revealed that democrats have criticized Ueland, a longtime GOP Senate aide and administration official during both Trump terms, saying he is too politically biased to lead the nonpartisan watchdog agency which conducts investigations and audits for Congress. They also remarked Republicans ignored a law that Democrats say requires the convening of a special legislative commission to make recommendations for the post.

    Recent findings suggest that ueland said if the Senate confirms him to lead the Government Accountability Office, “We can at the end of the day ... see a GAO which is more effective, which provides better information for Congress in a quicker way so Congress is able to take policy actions and drive change itself at this end of Pennsylvania Avenue.”.

    At the root of the partisan clash is a suspicion by Democrats that Trump is trying to install a puppet to lead an agency that has fought the administration repeatedly over the power of the purse and other matters.

    Democrats blasted Paul for rushing the hearing, which included a dozen other nominees for administration and judicial posts.

    “It’s so apparent that this is a box-checking exercise,” mentioned Sen. Gary Peters of Michigan, the ranking Democrat on the panel. “This committee is not doing due diligence, despite some of our members’ best efforts, because the chairman has chosen not to carry out his responsibility to provide advice and consent on nominations.”.

    Democrats remarked Paul did not allow Peters to make an opening statement at the hearing and restricted the amount of time given to senators to ask questions. A GOP aide disputed this, noting that Paul did not give an opening statement himself, Peters arrived late and all senators were given five minutes to ask questions.

    In a recent development, ueland has served as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget under Russ Vought, the OMB director. Trump nominated Ueland to head the GAO, a legislative branch agency, Monday.

    Democrats noted that the GAO has concluded multiple times that the administration violated the law by "impounding," or refusing to spend, appropriated funds. OMB has argued that the GAO misread the law and that it does not have any authority over the executive branch.

    Peters told Ueland that the GAO had issued 12 reports accusing the administration of violating the law, and he asked if Ueland agreed.

    Ueland did not give a direct response.

    Recent findings suggest that “First, many of those items indicated by those reports, I have not participated in,” he stated. Ueland said he had not reviewed the reports that Peters provided to him earlier, and that he would not offer an opinion on them.

    He also stated it was critical that he “not prejudge or come to this committee with informed conclusions about what it is that GAO has rendered as advice to Congress.” Ueland said he has a “clear commitment to follow the process.”.

    Peters noted when Ueland appeared before the committee last year after being nominated for the OMB post, he voiced support for the presidential authority of impoundment.

    Recent findings suggest that “We’re going to expect you to continue to basically ignore Congress,” Peters mentioned. “You’re going to be a rubber stamp for the administration.”.

    “That’s not so,” Ueland replied.

    Ueland remarked his experience as deputy overseeing the management side of OMB would be a “value add to GAO.” He cited his work “examining how the government actually functions, how it is organized, how it can be better optimized to deliver results.”.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, asked Ueland how he would grade GAO’s work to date.

    Ueland said he would give it a “medium grade over time.”.

    For example, he noted GAO has 38 government operations on a “high-risk list … some of which have been on there for 36 years.”.

    By contrast, Ueland referred to his work at OMB, where he mentioned “you have seen a very swift and aggressive effort by this administration in this term to set up systems and processes to ensure that we are not sending money out the door that we shouldn’t.”.

    Paul asked Ueland what he would do if administration officials told him they did not like a GAO investigation or conclusion.

    Ueland noted he would “fully follow through on charges from Congress and in the event of obstacles figure out ways to proceed to try to elicit information.” He said when he was a young staffer in the Senate, when there were disagreements between the legislative and executive branches, GAO and the administration had conversations “to see if there were appropriate paths forward.”.

    Responding to another question from Paul as to whether he would ignore a potential request from the White House to stop an investigation, Ueland said, “To be clear, yes.”.

    According to recent reports, sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., who is seeking to be the ranking Republican on the committee in the next Congress, stated he was satisfied that Republicans followed the letter of the law requiring a commission to make recommendations to the president for comptroller general. He added that he was not “completely sure they have followed the entire spirit of the law.”.

    It has been revealed that “For me, personally, Mr. Ueland is a great candidate in this role for GAO,” Lankford said.

    It has been revealed that paul sent three recommendations for comptroller general, including Ueland, to the White House last week from the six Republican members of a 10-member bipartisan, bicameral commission. But he never convened the body to seek applications from and interview candidates for the post.

    Industry observers note that and he gave the four Democrats on the commission less than 24 hours’ notice last week to offer their recommendations. Democrats charged that Paul subverted the process, and they did not offer recommendations.

    In a separate interview Wednesday, the president of the union that represents GAO employees decried the decision not to follow the commission process that characterized past comptroller general nominations.

    “We see that bipartisan process as extremely important to preserving and keeping the trust that GAO has with the entire Congress,” said Benjamin Emmel, president of Local 1921 of the International Federation of Professionals and Technical Engineers.

    Emmel, a senior analyst at GAO, said by sidestepping that procedure, “there is a cloud that hangs above any nominee where one party dominates that process.”.

    He said GAO’s credibility depends on members of both parties trusting that the organization is “nonpartisan, objective, independent and fair. If we lose that ability, we become less useful.”.

    The union is not advocating for or against Ueland or any nominee for the office. The Homeland Security panel is not expected to vote on the nominations until after Thanksgiving.

    On College Campuses, Nothing Is Free from Antisemitism

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that this month, Hunter College’s student government posted a flyer for Cultural Arts Night.
    • After several participating groups withdrew — seemingly because Hillel, a Jewish organization, was on the flyer — the student government’s president and vice president unveiled that the event “doesn’t align with our values or the values of the students we represent,” that it “should never have moved forward.” And, remarkably, she added, “To be blunt, we failed.”.
    • Shabbos Kestenbaum was the lead plaintiff in a federal antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard University, his alma mater.

    It has been revealed that this month, Hunter College’s student government posted a flyer for Cultural Arts Night. Six student groups would share one evening: the Peruvian Students Association, the Chinese Students and Scholars Association, the Taiwanese Student Association, Centro PR, Students for Justice in Palestine, and Hillel.

    After several participating groups withdrew — seemingly because Hillel, a Jewish organization, was on the flyer — the student government’s president and vice president unveiled that the event “doesn’t align with our values or the values of the students we represent,” that it “should never have moved forward.” And, remarkably, she added, “To be blunt, we failed.”.

    Shabbos Kestenbaum was the lead plaintiff in a federal antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard University, his alma mater.

    On “On College Campuses, Nothing Is Free from Antisemitism”.

    #157185. Sweeping permitting overhaul passes Senate, on to House

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1481 w)
